newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef traded higher on mostly moderate demand and offerings, USDA said. Increased retail and HRI demand was noted for immediate and future needs at the end of the trading period.
Chuck and round cuts traded sharply higher early in the week, but stalled by week's end. Rib and loin cuts traded higher with the biggest advances in the choice product.

Closely trimmed items traded higher on fairly good demand, especially for the chuck cuts, as these items continue to trend higher. Trade on beef trimmings was firm on light to moderate demand and offerings.
Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally steady on good demand for immediate and future needs as these items were seen as good values.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 1.50 to 5.00 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal 1.00 to 4.00 higher; Select and Choice round primal 2.50 higher; Select and Choice loin primal 1.00 to 2.00 higher; Closely trimmed items 1.50 to 2.50 higher; Beef trimmings 2.00 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items generally steady.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 2.57 at 107.07; 700/850 Up 2.13 at 105.66; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 1.52 at 101.26; 700/850 Up 1.48 at 100.56.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT: The boneless beef market traded lower again in a supply driven situation. Not only were slaughter cow numbers readily available, but the market was burdened by moderate to heavy supplies of lower lean percentage beef.

Demand was light to moderate despite the lower prices levels, as many grinders sought other grinding material. Moreover, the cow carcasses complex was lower in response to the declining boneless market and an abundant supplies.

Cow cuts traded mostly steady to weak on light demand for moderate to heavy offerings. Utility carcasses 1.00 lower; Cutter generally 1.00 lower. Fresh 90% boneless beef 2.00-4.00 lower; 85% 2.00 lower; 75% 1.50-2.00 lower; 65% steady. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, September 12, 1996 was estimated at 67.28 per cwt., down 1.75 from a week ago Friday.
